name: Syndrome with Difference of Sex Development of Gynecological Interest
aliases: Gynecological Difference of Sex Development Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Diagnosis of DSD Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous external genitalia at birth or in early childhood
Histopathological evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or atypical gonadal tissue
Abnormal serum levels of sex steroids and gonadotropins inconsistent with chromosomal sex
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with sex development
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of Müllerian or Wolffian duct anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia plus either gonadal dysgenesis or hormonal dysregulation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and imaging studies support but are not mandatory for diagnosis.

laboratory: Abnormal serum sex steroid levels (e.g., testosterone, estradiol)
Karyotype analysis showing sex chromosome anomalies
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound revealing Müllerian or Wolffian duct anomalies
MRI of pelvis showing gonadal position and structure
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as SRY, SOX9, NR5A1, WT1
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing dysgenesis or mixed gonadal tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Rapid virilization during infancy or childhood
Signs of gonadal tumor development such as gonadoblastoma
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD update: Consensus on diagnosis and treatment. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
Orphanet Report Series: Syndromes with difference of sex development of gynecological interest. Orphanet. 2023.
